questions.question: In an LP with two decision variables $x_1,x_2$, which condition makes a point a corner point?
options: At least one constraint boundary passes through it.
Two constraints hold with equality there, even if they give the same line.
Two constraint boundaries that are not parallel pass through it.
Every constraint of the LP holds with equality there.

questions.question: In an LP with two decision variables, the boundary lines of two of its constraints are not parallel and meet at a point $P$. When is $P$ a feasible corner point?
options: Always, since two nonparallel boundaries meet at $P$.
Only when every constraint of the LP is active at $P$.
Whenever both coordinates of $P$ are nonnegative.
When $P$ also satisfies all other constraints of the LP.

questions.question: An LP has constraints $a_{i1}x_1+a_{i2}x_2\le b_i$ ($i=1,\dots,m$) with every right-hand side $b_i\ge0$, together with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Why is $(0,0)$ a feasible corner point?
options: $x_1=0$ and $x_2=0$ meet there, and every constraint holds at $(0,0)$.
It is not one, since no functional constraint is active at $(0,0)$.
Every LP has the origin as a feasible corner, whatever its constraints.
The origin is feasible, and every feasible point on an axis is a corner.

questions.question: In an LP with three decision variables $x_1,x_2,x_3$, at least how many constraints, counting nonnegativity constraints, are active at a corner point?
options: 2, just as in an LP with two variables
1, the boundary on which the point lies
3, fixing a single point by their equations
All of them, so that no constraint has slack

questions.question: In an LP with two decision variables, the corner point $P$ is where the boundary lines of constraints A and B meet; the lines are not parallel. The right-hand side of A is increased slightly, and nothing else changes. What happens to $P$?
options: It stays put, since a corner depends only on the constraint coefficients.
It moves along A's shifted boundary, away from B's boundary line.
It disappears, since constraint A can no longer be active anywhere.
It moves along B's boundary line, to where A's shifted boundary meets it.

questions.question: An LP with variables $x_1,x_2\ge0$ has the constraints $x_1+2x_2\le8$ and $3x_1+x_2\le9$. At which point do the boundary lines of these two constraints intersect?
An LP has constraints $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1\le4$, $x_2\le5$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. The boundaries of $x_1\le4$ and $x_2\le5$ meet at $(4,5)$. Is $(4,5)$ a feasible corner point?
options: Yes: two nonparallel boundary lines meet at this point.
Yes: it satisfies both constraints whose boundaries define it.
No: it is a boundary intersection that violates $x_1+x_2\le6$.
No: it does not lie on the boundary line $x_1+x_2=6$.

questions.question: The feasible region of an LP is given by $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1\le3$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. How many feasible corner points does it have?
An LP has constraints $2x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1+x_2\le7$, $x_1\le4$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Is the feasible point $(3,4)$ a corner point, and which constraints are active there?
options: A corner: $2x_1+x_2\le10$ and $x_1+x_2\le7$ are both active.
Not a corner: $x_1\le4$ is not active at this point.
A corner, lying where the boundaries of $x_1\le4$ and $x_1+x_2\le7$ meet.
Not a corner: neither nonnegativity constraint is active.

questions.question: The feasible region of an LP is given by $x_1+x_2\le6$, $x_1\le4$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Which of these feasible points is not a corner point of the region?
In an LP with two decision variables, the constraint $x_1+x_2\le4$ is replaced by $x_1+x_2\ge4$, and nothing else changes. What happens to the boundary intersections that involve this constraint?
options: They are the same points, but their feasibility must be rechecked.
They move, since the constraint now points in the other direction.
They are the same points, and so are the feasible corner points.
They all become infeasible, as the region lies on the other side.

questions.question: Why does an LP with two decision variables and finitely many constraints have only finitely many corner points?
options: Its feasible region is always bounded, so it can only have finitely many corners.
Each corner comes from a pair of the finitely many lines, and a pair meets at most once.
Each constraint produces exactly one corner, so there are as many corners as constraints.
Only feasible points are counted as corners, and a feasible region has few of them.

questions.question: The feasible region given by $x_1+x_2\ge4$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is unbounded. What are its feasible corner points?
options: None, since only bounded regions have corner points
Only $(0,0)$, where both axis boundaries meet
$(4,0)$ and $(0,4)$; unboundedness does not matter
Every point on the line $x_1+x_2=4$ is one

questions.question: An LP in $x_1,x_2,x_3$ has constraints $x_1+x_2+x_3\le6$, $x_1\le2$ and $x_1,x_2,x_3\ge0$. Which of these points is a feasible corner point?
The feasible region of an LP is given by $x_1+x_2\ge4$, $x_1+3x_2\ge6$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Which points are its feasible corner points?
In an LP with variables $x_1,x_2$, which pair of constraint boundary lines determines a corner point?
In an LP with two decision variables, one constraint is deleted and all others are kept. What can happen to the set of feasible corner points?
options: Corners can only be added, since deleting a constraint lets the region grow.
Corners can only vanish, since fewer boundary lines are left to intersect.
Nothing, unless the deleted constraint was active at every corner.
Some may vanish and new ones may appear where intersections become feasible.

questions.question: In an LP with variables $x_1,x_2,x_3\ge0$, the feasible point $P=(1,3,0)$ has exactly three active constraints: $x_1+x_2\le4$, $2x_1+2x_2\le8$ and $x_3\ge0$. Is $P$ a corner point?
options: No; the first two give one equation, so only two independent ones remain.
Yes; three constraints are active, one for each of the three variables.
Yes; any feasible point on two different boundaries is a corner here.
No; a point with a zero coordinate always lies inside a boundary face.

questions.question: Three upper limits, $x_1+x_2\le4$, $x_1\le2$ and $x_2\le2$, together with $x_1,x_2\ge0$, define an LP region in the plane. Counting each point once, how many feasible corner points does this region have?
An LP has the constraints $x_1+x_2=4$, $x_1\le3$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$. Which points are its feasible corner points?
options: None; the equality is active everywhere
